newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Bond Exchange backs latest statistics.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Bond Exchange backs latest statistics.

text.p: The Bond Exchange on Monday backed its statistics which showed volumes topped 11 billion rand on Friday after foreigners bought a net one billion rand's worth of South African bonds.

Brokers earlier brought the data into question, arguing that the dearth of activity on the market as well as perceptions that there had been little foreign interest on Friday did not add up with the exchange's data.

Graeme Brookes, Bond Exchange company secretary, said the consternation over the data appeared to stem from the fact that many of the trades on Friday had been screen-based rather than through the floor.
"Some of the very big foreign players are taking some big blocks in the RSA stocks. The big volumes go through the screens and the floor does not see them," Brookes said.
"The floor does about 50 percent of reported trades, but their volumes on average are around 20 to 25 percent of the market and perhaps they are just tapering off a bit now," he said.
"We don't think the numbers lie. Our system is robust and we stand behind the figures," Brookes added.
